message: Kieran, I couldn't see any attached file. Please resend it so I can provide an accurate quote.
I'm reviewing it now; once that's done, I'll get back to you in a few minutes.
What estimated timeframe and budget are you considering? I can provide support with stamping your project.
My proposal is a turnaround of 6 business days for the review and stamp, at a fee of \$320, because the project change is very simple. Please let me know. Thanks.
Although the project is simple, the document runs 84 pages, so the earlier quote might be too low. Could we set the fee at $640-800 and complete it within the next 72-96 hours?
Kieran, I wanted to check: have you remained available?

Even though 84 pages may seem daunting, you really do not need to review all of them. I initially felt the same way, but the actual work is limited to reviewing the minor modifications listed in the word file. For this change, I am a licensed mechanical engineer, and my scope comes down to only the highlighted portion of the attached file. The electrical scope is similarly limited. If \$480 works for you, let’s finalize it at that amount and I will inform the client. Please advise.
Alright, let's move forward.
Before we can begin the work, please send a contract.
I will inform the client of our agreement. Once I receive confirmation, I will initiate the offer. Thanks.
Alright

For the attached project, the required deliverables are permit-ready Mechanical, Plumbing and Electrical drawings with an electrical PE stamp; I will handle the Mechanical and Plumbing stamps. Would you be available to support this additional work, and if so, what price and timeline would you quote?
I can provide support for that project as well.
What budget do you have in mind?
Could you propose a reasonable price? I will then check with the client to see whether it fits his budget.
When is the project expected to be ready to kick off? For the fee, I propose $750.
Can the provided description file explaining what changed be used as the basis for stamping, or does the client need to supply redline drawings?
Because it shows what was done in response to the previous comment, I consider a redlined drawing the best file to stamp.

I'll ask the client again. Just to confirm, this includes permit-ready Mechanical, Plumbing and Electrical drawings with all necessary load calculations, correct? T 24 is not needed, but HvAC sizing calculations are required. Could you also provide your California electrical PE license number? The project should kick off soon, no later than five weeks from now.
Given that I understood the scope to cover only review and stamping, could you clarify whether I am also expected to provide additional drawings and calculations?

Would pictures of the changes that align with the written description be sufficient? If you still require redlines, I will request them; I just want to determine the minimum documentation needed to kick off the project.

For kickoff, the minimum documentation I would typically require consists of the written scope of work, which has already been provided; photos of every modified area; the room numbers associated with each change; and any sketches, screenshots, or informal markups showing the approximate locations of the work.
The electrical PE is MERCER T DANIEL, and the license number is 47283.

To clarify the scope, you would create and stamp the electrical drawings, while I would stamp the mechanical drawings. You would also perform whatever calculations are required to produce the drawings; please confirm that this is within your competence. The applicable scope includes Manual. J, Manual S, and Manual D.
For this clarified scope, what price would you propose? Also, what timeline would you propose?

This clarified scope is within my capabilities. Assuming the architectural background files are complete and permit-ready, my estimate for the electrical permit drawings, PE stamp, required electrical calculations, and applicable Manual J/S/D calculations is $12,000–$18,000, with an approximate turnaround of 7–9 weeks. The scope is extensive.

That estimate seems high, so I am curious whether you have completed projects of a similar size and whether clients typically pay this much. I am asking because I do not want to accept a job that is too large to deliver, while also wanting to quote a price that is not completely outside the market range. Thanks for your help, Marisol.

Your pricing is not outside the market, since fees in that range are fairly typical when calculations, permit drawings, and PE stamping are included. Projects of similar size and complexity are within my experience. The important part is being comfortable with the scope and confident that you can support the project through permitting.
Once the client responds, I'll pass their feedback along. First, I'll present this pricing to them. Thanks.
My Pleasure
Kieran, could you let me know whether the project remains available?
Marisol, I've contacted the client. Their response is what I'm currently waiting for.
Understood. Your response is what I'll be waiting for as well.
I'll keep you informed once I have an update.
Great
Could you let me know, Kieran, whether the client has provided an update?

Marisol, the client's latest response says that a formal offer is being sent, the electrical redlines are still outstanding, and the pictures have been received. I have not received the formal offer yet and am waiting for it. Thanks.
Does this update mean that we are still involved in the project, and what does it mean for us?
I will contact you if the client responds. Given how slow he has been to reply, however, I would not rely on that; he may still contact me after receiving the redline. Thank you!
Alright

Marisol, I hope you are doing well. The client contacted me to ask whether you can stamp the changes without redlines, possibly by adding a letter describing the change you are approving. Is that feasible? If it is, I can send you the formal offer. Please also resend the PE name and license number, because I am seeing different information for Nevada PE license 47283 on the PE website. Thanks, Kieran.
Yes, that stamping and letter approach is feasible. Thanks for getting back to me.
Could you write the letter so that I can stamp it together with the other materials?
For clarity, I was not the person who sent license # 47283.
We will use MERRICK NOLAN's electrical PE license 038617 to stamp your project.
Since the scope now includes a stamped letter, would it be possible to increase the budget to $620?
For easy reference, I’ve reattached the word file containing the changes, Marisol. Thanks.
Since the PE stamp was included from the outset, could we cap the amount at \$540?
Alright
Please submit the formal offer.
For confirmation, could you please send the plan again?
I’ve attached it; please let me know if you have any questions.
Some pages already show a stamp. For clarity, which pages should receive the electrical stamp?

Before this project’s changes, the as-built drawings were captured in the .pdf copy. The project’s electrical revisions appear in the word file you are reviewing and approving so the as-built electrical sheets can be amended.

Whichever option is more convenient, you may either add a cover letter and stamp the word file, or redline the existing pdf and stamp those marked-up sheets to confirm your concurrence with the changes.
I think the better option is to prepare a cover letter stating that the work is done and stamp the word file.
To verify that the completed work matches what is specified in the word file, I’ve asked the client to provide pictures of the changes.
Correct
Alright—I will update you soon.
Thanks
Greetings, Kieran.
Hello there, Marisol.
The project has been completed.
When will the second milestone be activated? I wanted to check.

Once the client accepts the delivery, I’ll complete the second milestone. I retained it to incorporate any client or city comments if the stamped method is rejected or they request changes to the confirmation method.
Although I conservatively set the date as Oct 14, I do not expect it to take that long.

Understood. After I deliver the stamped word document, you can approve the first milestone and activate the second. You won’t release payment for the second milestone until you have provided confirmation, so this sequence protects both of us.
Before I have this letter stamped, please review it and identify any corrections needed in the wording.
I’ll review it and get back to you. The quick turnaround is appreciated, Marisol—thanks.
my pleasure
So that you can activate the second milestone, please release payment for the letter and stamped note.
Because I’m currently traveling and not at a computer, I’ll review it as soon as I have an opportunity and then release the payment as well.
okay
Thanks
During a stop in my travels, Marisol, I was able to review the letter. It looks good, but the PE stamp is missing; could you please sign it and return it to me?
For the item referenced here, could you please apply the stamp? Thanks.
Yes—once you release the first payment and activate the second milestone, I’ll provide the stamped letter.
i will send without delay
The payment has now been released—perfect, thank you.
The second milestone still hasn’t been activated. Activating it would show me that I’m waiting for your confirmation with the city.
Kieran, are you there? Hello?
I stepped away for a few minutes—sorry. It should be active now; is it showing as active for you? Please confirm.
Attached is the letter with its stamp.
Marisol, the signature block still reads “licensed professional's name.” Please replace that placeholder with the full legal name. Thanks.
okay
Please revise the date as well: it currently reads 09/11/2026, but it must use the US date format and appear as 11/09/2026.
Is everything okay now?
The revisions work, thank you.
We’re waiting to hear back from the client.

Marisol, I hope you’re doing well. We’ve received the client’s electrical notes: the stamped note was good, and the drawings were fine except that certain items needed to be called out. I’ve included the client’s request along with the information from the electrician. Since these callouts are part of the original scope and merely present it in greater detail, could you please stamp them? Thank you.
I appreciate your revision, but this requires additional stamps and was not part of our initial scope, as you know.

Marisol, thank you for responding. These callouts contain the same material you stamped in the letter; the only change is that content formerly presented as written annotations now appears on schematic sheets. You can verify the match because each callout heading in your letter corresponds to the description shown in the schematic.

Please reconsider and stamp these original-scope callouts in a schematic layout. This work belongs to the second milestone for addressing the city’s and client’s comments.

Thank you in advance for your support.
Many thanks, I appreciate it!
Could the pending payment be released immediately now?
Understood. As soon as I receive client sign-off, I will release the payment myself; although the milestone lists approval by the municipality, I will not wait for it.
Kieran, how have you been? I’m still waiting to hear from you about the project.
